recent.title: Early-Phase IND Protocol Recommendations for Solid Tumors; Draft Guidance for Industry; Availability
recent.ai_summary: FDA가 'Early-Phase IND Protocol Recommendations for Solid Tumors' 가이드라인 초안의 공고를 냈다. 고형암 대상 first-in-human 등 초기 임상 IND 프로토콜에 대한 권고이며 혈액암 치료제는 다루지 않는다고 한다. 초안이며 수집 자료는 관보 요약으로, 가이드라인 본문과 의견 제출 기한은 확인되지 않았다.
recent.source_summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) is announcing the availability of a draft guidance for industry titled "Early-Phase IND Protocol Recommendations for Solid Tumors." The purpose of this draft guidance is to provide recommendations to sponsors and clinical investigators developing early-phase trials, which include first-in- human (FIH) protocols or protocols for drugs and biologic products with limited human experience, submitted under an Investigational New Drug Application (IND) to the appropriate disease-specific division located within the Office of Oncologic Diseases (OOD) in the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER) and the Office of Clinical Evaluation (OCE) in the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER.) This draft guidance is specific to solid tumors and does not address protocols for investigational drugs intended to treat hematologic malignancies.

recent.source_summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency), is announcing a request for information (RFI) from interested parties to share perspectives on patient-level data access related to the use of real-world evidence (RWE) in regulatory decision-making for drugs and biological product submissions. The purpose of this RFI is to solicit input from interested parties on innovative solutions to address the challenges in submitting patient-level data for real-world data (RWD) analyzed in clinical studies included in a marketing application. Interested parties may include regulated industry, health information technology (HIT) vendors, academic medical centers, electronic data capture vendors, patient advocates, and other interested parties.

recent.source_summary: Geneva, 12 November 2026: The PIC/S Committee adopted the revised Pharmaceutical Inspection Co-operation Scheme (PIC/S 1/95 (Rev. 7)) at its meeting on 2 November 2026 in Istanbul, Türkiye. The revised Scheme entered into force on the same date. The PIC Scheme serves as the legal basis and institutional framework for PIC/S as a non-profit association established under Swiss law. It governs the organisation and functioning of PIC/S and establishes a legally non-binding arrangement for co-operation between its Members.
